distinguishing_from: vs login_required: FT returns 200 at the ORIGINAL article URL with the article title replaced by 'Subscribe to read'; a login wall redirects to a distinct /login URL.
notes: Full-body replacement paywall (Zephr). The response headers are decisive: x-host names a barrier-page origin and Set-Cookie carries an explicit DENIED access decision. Header evidence beats body evidence here.

distinguishing_from: vs gdpr_consent: THE SAME FILE is also the gdpr_consent sample. Consent and paywall co-occur on EU publishers; a classifier must be able to emit both, or it will mislabel one as the other.
notes: Teaser paywall: real headline and lede are present, the rest is truncated. NOTE THE PARSING TRAP - isAccessibleForFree is the STRING "False", not the boolean false. A naive JSON-LD check for a false boolean misses it. Same fetch as gdpr_consent/lemonde_article.html; file copied, not re-requested.

distinguishing_from: Attempted as paywall_news, actually served a DataDome captcha. Filed under captcha/datadome_captcha_nytimes.html.
notes: NYT, WSJ (robots-disallowed anyway), Economist and Washington Post all refuse plain curl before any paywall logic runs. WaPo reset the TCP connection outright (curl error 56). To collect a real NYT/WaPo paywall body you need a real browser engine; the bot layer fires first.
